card.name: Conditional words before benefit-justifies-risk
card.fires_on: The linking word (whom, when, if) that opens a restriction clause in use-only-if-needed statements, such as 'for whom alternatives are inadequate' or 'only when the benefit outweighs the risk'.

modes.label: for whom
modes.description: The word whom after 'patients for' in advice to reserve combined prescribing for cases lacking alternatives.
modes.example: reserve concomitant prescribing of these drugs for use in patients for<< whom>> alternative treatment options are inadequate.

modes.label: only when/if
modes.description: The word when or if after 'only' in pregnancy statements that allow use if benefit outweighs risk.
modes.example: Penicillamine should be used in women of childbearing potential only<< when>> the expected benefits outweigh the possible hazards.

card.plain: It marks the small word that starts a clause limiting a drug to cases where its benefit justifies the risk.
